title: The Giants of the Narrow Way

content:
Today we continue from Numbers chapter thirteen. Yesterday we studied how Moses sent twelve leaders to spy out the land of Canaan. They walked through the land for forty days. They saw the mountains, the valleys, the fortified cities, the strong people, and the sons of Anak. They also saw the fruits of the land. They cut down one great cluster of grapes from the valley of Eshcol, and two men carried it on a pole between them. They also brought back pomegranates and figs.

Numbers 13:27 says, "This was their report to Moses: 'We entered the land you sent us to explore, and it is indeed a bountiful country; a land flowing with milk and honey. Here is the kind of fruit it produces.'" The land was exactly as Yahweh had promised. It was not a dry promise. It was not an empty promise. It was a real land with real fruit, real abundance, and real blessing. The spies carried the fruit in their own hands. Their own eyes had seen that Yahweh's word was true. But ten of those spies looked at the same land and became afraid. They saw the fruit, yet they focused on the giants. They saw the promise, yet they magnified the fortified cities. They saw the goodness of Yahweh, yet they spoke more about the strength of man. Numbers 13:31 says, "But the other men who had explored the land with him disagreed. 'We can't go up against them! They are stronger than we are!'"

And this is where the spiritual lesson becomes very strong for us, the New Creation. Yahweh has also given us great and precious promises. He has not called us to wander without hope. He has promised us a home, a kingdom, a throne, immortality, and a place with Christ. We are not walking the narrow way for nothing. There is a promised inheritance set before us. Our Master said, "There is more than enough room in my Father's home. If this were not so, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?" (John 14:2). Paul speaks of immortal life and says, "For our dying bodies must be transformed into bodies that will never die; our mortal bodies must be transformed into immortal bodies" (1 Corinthians 15:53). Christ also promises a throne to the overcomers, saying, "Those who are victorious will sit with me on my throne, just as I was victorious and sat with my Father on his throne" (Revelation 3:21). And Peter tells us that Yahweh has given us promises that are exceedingly great and precious, "And because of his glory and excellence, he has given us great and precious promises" (2 Peter 1:4).

These promises are our promised land. We have not yet entered fully into them, but we have seen them by faith through Yahweh's Word. The spies saw Canaan with their eyes. We see our inheritance through the Scriptures, through the shadows, through the prophecies, through the words of Christ, through the promises of resurrection, and through the testimony of the apostles, through our spiritual eyes. Hebrews 11:13 says of the faithful ones, "They agreed that they were foreigners and nomads here on earth." They saw the promises from afar. They did not possess everything immediately, but they believed Yahweh. In the same way, we see the promised land from the Word. We see the shadow and the reality. We see the prophecy and the fulfilment. We see the invitation and the reward. But we are still walking toward it.

Yet, like the ten spies, some may begin to fear the path. The road to the promise is not a broad and easy one. Our Master said, "The gateway to life is very narrow and the road is difficult, and only a few ever find it" (Matthew 7:14). This road is difficult, but not because Yahweh is cruel. It is difficult because the flesh must be denied, pride must be put to death, anger must be controlled, jealousy must be cleansed, and selfishness must be laid down. The old man cannot enter the promised inheritance. The new man must be formed in us. Paul says, "Put on your new nature, created to be like God; truly righteous and holy" (Ephesians 4:24).

And to show the character of Christ in this present world is not easy at all.
It means loving when others hate. It means forgiving when others wound us.It means remaining silent when we long to defend ourselves. It means blessing when others curse. It means refusing revenge when our flesh cries out for justice on our own terms. It means speaking truth when lies would be far easier.It means keeping ourselves separate when a small compromise would make life comfortable. Our Master said, "Love your enemies! Pray for those who persecute you!" (Matthew 5:44). Peter said of him, "He did not retaliate when he was insulted, nor threaten revenge when he suffered" (1 Peter 2:23).And Paul says, "Don't be selfish; don't try to impress others. Be humble, thinking of others as better than yourselves" (Philippians 2:3).

These are not small lessons. These are the giants in the land. The giants in our lives are the betrayal of a friend we trusted, the relative who mocks our faith at every family gathering, the co-worker who takes credit for our work and smiles while doing it, the harsh word from a brother in the very congregation where we expected love, the neighbour who spreads a story about us that is not true, the child who will not listen no matter how much we pray, the illness that does not go away, the prayer that seems to receive no answer for years, the temptation that returns again and again in a private moment, the pride that rises when we are corrected, the tongue that wants to answer back before we can stop it, the quiet hurt of watching another brother or sister blessed and honoured while our own service goes unnoticed, and the loneliness of standing apart from a world that calls us strange for refusing its celebrations and its ways. These look enormous when we stand in front of them. But in reality they are not giants at all. They only appear big because we are measuring them against ourselves, and next to our own strength everything looks impossible. When we measure them against Yahweh, they shrink to their true size.

The betrayal is real, but Yahweh is greater. The temptation is strong, but Christ is stronger. The waiting is long, but the promise is sure. Not one of these things is able to stop a new creature who leans on the strength of God rather than his own. Yet because these giants look so large, some become afraid of the narrow way. They begin to say, "This is too hard. We cannot live like this. We cannot forgive like this. We cannot be separate like this. We cannot carry this cross." And like the ten spies, they say, "We are not able. "But in that whole camp, while ten men were spreading their fear and the people were beginning to lose heart, there was one man who had walked the very same land, seen the very same giants, and measured the very same walls; and yet he opened his mouth and said something completely different. His few words would echo through the rest of Scripture, and they show us exactly how the New Creation must face every giant on this narrow road. What did Caleb say, and where did his courage come from? That is where we will continue tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our Father,

We thank You for the great and precious promises You have set before us.

You have not called us to wander without hope, but toward a sure inheritance.

We confess that the giants of this narrow road often look larger than they truly are.

Teach us to forgive, to love, to stay pure, and to serve, even when it is hard.

Do not let us stand at the border of Your promise and say, 'We are not able.'

"I am certain that God, who began the good work within you, will continue his work until it is finally finished." Philippians 1:6

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
